findings.evidence: Lines 78-79 vs. 248-251; the author already needed `rw [totalOrder_apply, …]` at line 158 to cross between the two forms inside the file.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from `totalOrder_apply` (keep it as the `*_def` restatement) so `totalOrder` is the normal form; `map_add`/`map_zero` are already `@[simp mid, grind =]` in Mathlib (`Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean:325`) and keep `totalOrder (a + b)` simplifying. Alternatively state the whole API with `.1 + .2` and drop the bundled hom — but not both.
findings.issue: `@[simp] totalOrder_apply : totalOrder d = d.1 + d.2` makes the unfolded form the simp normal form, but every other lemma and field in the file is stated with `totalOrder`: `totalOrder_compositeDeg` (114), `totalOrder_le_totalOrder_compositeDeg` (119), `length_le_totalOrder_compositeDeg` (126), `finite_compositeDeg_le` (139), `totalOrder_pos_of_finite_compositeDeg_le` (154), `finite_deg_le_of_finite_compositeDeg_le` (166), `finite_compositeDeg_le_iff` (174), `finite_gradedPiece` (199), the `PowerCounting.totalOrder_pos`/`finite_deg_le` fields (218, 220), `PowerCounting.finite_compositeDeg_le` (239), and the `@[simp]` lemma `mem_truncation` (249) whose RHS simp then rewrites further. Since `totalOrder` has no `@[expose]`, downstream the two forms are bridged only by this lemma, so after any `simp` a goal is in `(…).1 + (…).2` shape where `mem_truncation`, `truncation_mono`, `mem_truncation_totalOrder` and `mul_mem_truncation` no longer apply.

findings.evidence: Line 269-270; compare `ofFinite_deg` (232) and `mem_truncation` (248), which are annotated.
findings.issue: `truncation_zero : P.truncation 0 = {1}` is a closed-form value of a normal-form LHS and is not `@[simp]`.

findings.evidence: `PowerCounting.finite_compositeDeg_le` at line 239 is the only specialization in the namespace; `finite_gradedPiece` (199) and `gradedPiece` (185) have no `P`-level counterpart; roadmap `QuarkoniaAndExotics/README.md:384` and acceptance example 1 at line 1246.
findings.fix: Add `PowerCounting.finite_gradedPiece`, `PowerCounting.coe_truncation` (immediate from `Set.Finite.coe_toFinset`), and the inclusion of a graded piece into the truncation at its own total order.
findings.issue: The `PowerCounting` namespace develops only the truncation side: it specializes `finite_compositeDeg_le` to `P` but has no parallel `P.finite_gradedPiece`, even though `gradedPiece`/`finite_gradedPiece` are listed as main results and "finiteness of each graded piece" is the roadmap's headline for 0.2. A consumer holding `P` must write `Quarkonium.finite_gradedPiece P.deg P.totalOrder_pos P.finite_deg_le d`. There is also no lemma linking the two layers (`gradedPiece P.deg d ⊆ ↑(P.truncation (totalOrder d))`) and no `coe_truncation : ↑(P.truncation n) = {o | totalOrder (compositeDeg P.deg o) ≤ n}`, so the `Set`-level results the file proves cannot be applied to the `Finset` without re-deriving the coercion by hand.

summary: The surface is minimal and bodies are unexposed, but `@[simp] totalOrder_apply` destroys the `totalOrder` abstraction that every other lemma in the file is stated in, and the `PowerCounting` layer carries only the truncation half of the API (no graded-piece specialization, no `coe_truncation`, no `simp` on `truncation_zero`).
